units: <cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 8:1">B. Kam. VIII, 1</cite>, v. <cite ref="N00461"><he>נֵזֶק</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 84a:11">Ib. 84ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Bava Kamma 26b:2">26ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Exodus 21:25">Ex. XXI, 25</cite>) <he>ליתן צ׳ במקום נזק</he> this intimates that you must decree indemnity for pain even where injury has been inflicted (in addition to damages for mayhem).
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 19b">Snh. 19ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>צ׳ גידול בנים</he>, v. <cite ref="C00635"><he>גִּידּוּל</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Taanit 11a:5-6">Taan. 11ᵃ</cite> <he>בזמן … שרוי בצ׳</he> when the community is in trouble (and holds a fast).

<cite ref="Taanit 11a:8">Ib.</cite> <he>הואיל וישראל שרויין בצ׳ … עמהם בצ׳</he> as Israel is in trouble (suffering the privations of warfare), I (Moses), too, will suffer privations with them, v. <cite ref="R00661"><he>צָעַר</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Taanit 10b:4">Ib. 10ᵇ</cite> <he>בדבר של צ׳ עושה … צ׳ הוא לו</he> in a matter of affliction, one may act (as if he were a distinguished person) …, for his motive is not self-elevation but affliction (sympathy with public sufferings).
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 52">Gen. R. s. 52</cite>, end <he>צַעֲרוֹ של איש וכ׳</he> the privation (abstinence from sexual contact) is felt more intensely by the man than by the woman.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 31a:21">B. Mets. 31ᵃ</cite> <he>משום דאיכא צ׳ בעלי חיים</he> because there is suffering of animals connected with the case (which must be relieved).
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 32b:17">Ib. 32ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Shabbat 128b:7">Sabb. 128ᵇ</cite> <he>צ׳ בעלי חיים דאורייתא</he> the duty of relieving the suffering of beasts is a Biblical law; a. v. fr.
